back: Letters added to the beginning of a word to change its meaning, e.g. un-happy, re-write, mis-spell.
notes: A prefix does not usually change the word class.

back: Letters added to the end of a word, usually to change its word class, e.g. kind → kindness, care → careful.

front: Choosing in-, im-, il- or ir-
back: im- before m and p (immature, impossible); il- before l (illegal); ir- before r (irregular); in- elsewhere (incorrect).
notes: Un- and dis- are separate prefixes that must be learnt word by word.
kindness, payment, decision, ability, childhood, friendship.
careful, careless, reliable, famous, active, national, scientific, rainy.

back: -er/-or = the person who does the action (employer); -ee = the person who receives it (employee).
-ing describes what causes a feeling (a boring lesson); -ed describes how someone feels (bored pupils).
strong → strength, long → length, deep → depth, proud → pride, pronounce → pronunciation, maintain → maintenance.
